clue.text: Being nearly crazy helps pub staff

indicators.note: nearly means the word for crazy stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad or crazy
aids is a verb meaning helps or assists

explanation.surface: Bar workers are said to be half mad, which only helps them do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is everyday British slang for crazy; cut short it leaves the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who serve drinks behind a bar are a pub's serving staff, so the plural fits a staff.

clue.text: When work's subject to error, see supervisor

indicators.note: subject to places the work below the error in this down entry

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake
op is short for opus, a work; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: If a job contains a mistake, go and consult the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, so the one who oversees a see is the answer; bish is British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop has charge of a diocese, which is called a see, so he oversees it.

clue.text: The facts of life shook Israelite

indicators.note: shook means the letters of the word Israelite are shaken up into a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word are the anagram fodder, used as written

explanation.surface: An Israeli citizen is shocked to learn the facts of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Realities are things as they actually exist, the hard facts one must accept.

clue.text: Publican's mate possibly serving fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ale plus wife, the wife of someone selling ale
second meaning: a North American fish of the herring family

explanation.walkthrough: Taken apart, the word suggests the landlady of an alehouse; whole, it is a herring-like fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word historically meant a woman who kept an alehouse and also names an Atlantic food fish related to herring.

clue.text: Deal with later yield

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to postpone, put off
second meaning: to submit or give way to someone else

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a plan to handle profits later, but each phrase is a separate meaning of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both postponing an action and submitting respectfully to another person's judgement.

clue.text: Lengthy statement of religious belief at end of mass

indicators.note: at signals that the belief sits at that point, right after the letter
the end of the word mass is its last letter, which here comes first

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
a creed is a formal statement of religious belief

explanation.surface: A long recital of faith said at the close of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the creed recited in church, but the definition is only the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing or speech, so a lengthy statement.

clue.text: Item attached to end of bar is connecting rod

parts.note: an item is a romantic couple

indicators.note: the end of the word bar is its last letter

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A mechanic describes a fitting on the tip of a bar that links parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Item looks like a mechanical part, but it is the slang sense of two people in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupler is a device or rod that joins two parts, such as railway carriages, together.

clue.text: Be leader no longer?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer holding a role
the leader is 1st, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A deposed chief wonders whether to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1st is read as the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being or reality.

clue.text: What's been laid badly? It's open to question

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of been laid are arranged poorly, so reordered

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged, as written

explanation.surface: Paving or carpet that was put down poorly may be disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deniable can be disputed or denied, so it is questionable.

clue.text: People who eat and drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: those who champ, chewing noisily
second meaning: British slang for champagne

explanation.walkthrough: To champ is to munch; the same word is British slang for champagne. The near-twin CHOMPERS fits the first sense but is not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is colloquial for champagne, and literally names those who champ or chew their food.

clue.text: Annual assessment by marriage guidance counsellor?

definitions.meaning: the US President's yearly address to Congress reviewing the nation
read literally, someone who would assess how a marriage, a union, is faring

explanation.walkthrough: The President's yearly speech takes stock of the nation; a counsellor would take stock of a couple's union, so one phrase serves both.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the American President's yearly speech reviewing the country's condition, and also literally the condition of a marriage.

clue.text: Type of blood supplied to organ I cut into in theatre

parts.note: O is one of the blood groups

indicators.note: cut into means the letter I goes inside the organ's name

parts.note: the liver is an organ of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A transfusion at the hospital during an operation in the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an operating theatre; the definition is a London stage, the Olivier Theatre at the National Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olivier is the largest auditorium of London's National Theatre, named after the actor Laurence Olivier.

clue.text: Reservists from island fired into receding target

indicators.note: into means the island and fired words go inside the target word
receding means the word for target runs backwards, moving away

parts.note: an aim is a target
lit means set on fire, fired

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers from an island firing at a target that moves away from them.
explanation.walkthrough: Fired looks like gunfire but means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers called on in emergencies, much like reserve forces.

clue.text: Its length one associated with cats?

definitions.meaning: the span of something, here how long one exists
cats are said to have nine lives, so each of them would have that span

explanation.walkthrough: Cats proverbially have nine lives; the span of just one of them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifetime is the duration of a single life, and a cat supposedly gets nine of these.

clue.text: Recognise one has depression, even though variable

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a dent is a hollow or depression
if can mean although, as in a pleasant if long day
y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Spotting that someone is depressed even though their mood varies.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression suggests low mood, but it is a dip in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify someone is to recognise who they are or establish their identity.

clue.text: Charge pound for one wanting honey

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper names a price per pound for anyone who wants to buy honey.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, an animal famous for raiding bees' nests to eat honey.

clue.text: Target man horribly? She might

indicators.note: horribly means the letters of target man are mangled into a fresh order

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged, as written

explanation.surface: Who would pick on a man cruelly? A certain kind of woman would.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters are rearranged, and the scolding woman they spell is just the sort to victimise a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing, quarrelsome woman, a shrew who might well bully a husband.

clue.text: Type of error made if man's. involved in dubious call

indicators.note: involved in places the man's name inside the scrambled call
dubious means the letters of call are shaky, so rearranged

parts.note: this word supplies the letters that are rearranged around the name
Eric stands for a man's name; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A slip that occurs when someone misjudges a doubtful decision.
explanation.walkthrough: The man is any male first name; Eric fits. A clerical error is a typing or copying slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerical error is a mistake made in copying or record-keeping, office work done by clerks.

clue.text: Young woman has a sort of fever

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl has come down with a feverish illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a viral disease named after the Nigerian town where it was first identified.

clue.text: In a way, teacher's lost heart to another scholar

indicators.note: in means the shortened teacher sits inside a plus the word for way

parts.note: taken as written
St is short for street, a way

indicators.note: lost heart means the teacher's middle letter is dropped

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A dispirited teacher yields to a rival academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Another links back to the teacher in the surface: a different kind of learned person.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a scholar who specialises in Arabic language and culture.

clue.text: Blade shaped three points with a single style

parts.note: E, N and S are three compass points
a single one is I, the Roman numeral
form can mean style or manner

explanation.surface: A fencing or design note about a blade shaped with three tips in one style.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensiform is a botanical term meaning sword-shaped, as in the long leaves of an iris.

clue.text: Skill needed to come across county avoiding tails

indicators.note: avoiding tails says each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: to come across something is to find it
Essex is an English county east of London

explanation.surface: Some talent is required to cross a county while steering clear of its tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding tails' docks both words: FIND loses D and ESSEX loses X, leaving FIN + ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is refined delicacy or adroitness in handling something, a kind of skill.

clue.text: Negotiate with bankrupt head of republic

parts.note: broke means penniless, bankrupt

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of republic

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Holding talks with the penniless leader of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To broker a deal is to arrange or negotiate it as an intermediary.

clue.text: Take a break before painting, then begin again

parts.note: to rest is to take a break
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: An artist pauses before picking up the brushes and starting over.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start once more, to resume after stopping.

clue.text: Shoot in heart of country out of season

indicators.note: out of means the middle letter is taken away from the season

parts.note: spring is a season of the year

indicators.note: the heart of country is its central letter

parts.note: a seven-letter word whose single middle letter is taken

explanation.surface: A young plant appears in the countryside before its proper time.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of season reads as untimely, but it means taken out of the season's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or shoot with leaves, cut from a plant.

clue.text: Female's not just come here for amusement

parts.note: unfair means not just, unjust

explanation.surface: A woman complains it is unjust she was dragged along to have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is and acts as a link; the definition describes a place where people go to be entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is a travelling show of rides and stalls, a place people visit purely to enjoy themselves.

clue.text: Northern waterfall producing power

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in northern England a waterfall is a ..., from Old Norse

explanation.walkthrough: Waterfalls in the Lake District and Yorkshire Dales are called forces, as in High Force; the surface pictures hydroelectric power.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means strength or energy, and in northern English dialect it names a waterfall.

clue.text: Ground needs placard, if farm's parking in short supply

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is supplied, so the answer is buried within those words

parts.note: the answer runs through these words, from the end of placard into parking

explanation.surface: A sign at the field warns that parking at the farm is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground is a sports stadium: Cardiff Arms Park is the famous Welsh rugby ground in Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports venue is called a ground in British usage, and this is the historic home of Welsh rugby.

clue.text: Sign about piece to be played smoothly

indicators.note: about means the star sign goes around the word for a piece

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
piece is slang for a gun, as is gat

explanation.surface: A musical direction about how to play a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Piece suggests a piece of music, but it is gangster slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is an Italian musical direction telling the performer to play the notes smoothly and connected.

clue.text: Sees term differently, but really it's the same

definitions.note: the answer is the same thing as a term, the clue word just before

indicators.note: differently means the letters of those two words are set out in another order

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged, as written

explanation.surface: Someone views a word in a new light, though it means the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at term: the rearranged letters spell another word for an academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year division of the academic year, much the same as a school or university term.
